01-queue.alt: The MENATER triage queue: two alerts waiting on a human at the top, then closed cases, each row carrying severity, verdict, confidence and time taken.
01-queue.cap: The triage queue. Anything waiting on a human rises to the top and carries the accent — the one colour reserved for someone must act. Real screenshot: this install has no model key, hence the fallback verdict on every row.

05-lookup.alt: The Lookup tab after querying 8.8.8.8: a verdict reading “nothing against it”, the line “1 of 4 sources answered”, and two source cards marked “not asked”.
05-lookup.cap: A verdict that states its own scope. One source answered, and the panel says so beside the verdict; the two sources with no key are not asked — a question nobody put, not a hole in what is known.

04-case.alt: An incident card for a critical ransomware alert: fallback verdict at confidence 0, four pipeline steps with their timings, and an approval block proposing an escalation.
04-case.cap: One incident. The verdict names its own cause, the destination is — because the detection recorded none, and the proposed action sits behind Approval required. Nothing was executed.

03-tracking.alt: The Tracking tab: 120 runs inspected, 118 attached to an alert, a warning that the observed window is full, and three sub-tabs for processing chains, orphan runs and the run log.
03-tracking.cap: The unreduced view. It counts the runs the queue could not show you, and warns when the observed window is full — beyond it, the console does not know — rather than letting a bounded read look like a complete one.

02-ingestion.alt: The Ingestion tab: three delivery architectures side by side with their costs stated, hybrid selected, and a table mapping P1 to P4 onto webhook or polling with the delay each implies.
02-ingestion.cap: Choosing a delivery architecture. Each option states what it buys and what it costs, and the lane table quotes half a polling interval — the average added delay, not the interval, because that is the number a P1 gets weighed against.

06-code.alt: The Code tab: a four-stage strip reading “reading your code”, “hunting for holes”, “second opinion”, “your report”, then a target picker offering a folder, a single file or a GitHub repository, and a choice between the whole project and only what changed.
06-code.cap: Code scanning. The four stages are named before anything runs, and the scope question says outright which choice costs more.

07-health.alt: The connectivity test results: a red banner reading “at least one link is broken, 9 checks green, 5 to watch, 1 failing, 0 undetermined — in 14 ms”, then per-check rows for the database, the SQL schema, the triage model key and four enrichment sources.
07-health.cap: The connectivity test on the same install. Nine green, five to watch, one failing, zero undetermined — four states, so “checking” is never reported as “broken”. Each line names the consequence and then the fix: the missing model key says every alert will take the fail-safe verdict, and where to put the key.
